title: Explore How Texas Housing Markets Weathered the 2008 Financial Crisis
text: package includes one dataset, tx_housing_markets: monthly sales, prices, listings inventory 46 Texas market areas January 2000 July 2015. Housing data: collected Texas &M University (TAMU) Real Estate Center (https://trerc.tamu.edu/), using copy distributed ggplot2 package ggplot2::txhousing. Inflation data: Consumer Price Index US South region (CUUR0300SA0) US Bureau Labor Statistics, retrieved FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CUUR0300SA0). used convert median prices July 2015 dollars, prices different years can compared fairly. script data-raw/tx_housing_markets.R prepares data: renames city area (since many counties regions), converts decimal years proper monthly dates, labels month pre-crisis (2000-2006), downturn (2007-2010) recovery (2011-2015), joins inflation data calculate inflation-adjusted median prices. recreate dataset, run source("data-raw/tx_housing_markets.R") package’s source folder. See ?tx_housing_markets description every column. Limitations: data end July 2015, later recoveries captured; market areas MLS (multiple listing service) regions rather exact city boundaries; two areas (Kerrville South Padre Island) data 2007, fall recovery measured.

code: crisis_recovery(measure = "sales", areas = c("Austin", "Dallas", "Houston")) |>   dplyr::select(area, drop_pct, recovery_year, status) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   area    drop_pct recovery_year status                #>   <chr>      <dbl>         <int> <chr>                 #> 1 Austin     -34.4          2013 Recovered             #> 2 Dallas     -34              NA Not recovered by 2015 #> 3 Houston    -29.9          2014 Recovered             # How far home sales fell in three large markets, and whether they recovered  crisis_recovery(measure = "median_real") |>   dplyr::slice_min(drop_pct, n = 5) |>   dplyr::select(area, peak_year, low_year, drop_pct, status) #> # A tibble: 5 × 5 #>   area        peak_year low_year drop_pct status                #>   <chr>           <int>    <int>    <dbl> <chr>                 #> 1 Galveston        2006     2009    -32.3 Not recovered by 2015 #> 2 Garland          2002     2010    -27.8 Not recovered by 2015 #> 3 Brownsville      2005     2009    -20.6 Not recovered by 2015 #> 4 Laredo           2004     2010    -19.8 Not recovered by 2015 #> 5 Harlingen        2000     2010    -19.7 Not recovered by 2015 # The five areas with the biggest fall in inflation-adjusted prices
